synthcheck

Experimental. synthcheck checks how authentic synthetic survey respondents are: Whether respondents generated by large language models resemble the real people they are meant to stand in for.

It looks at three things:

  • Overlap: Do synthetic respondents land where real people land?
  • Structure: Do the items relate to each other as they do in real people?
  • Behaviour (coming next): Do synthetic respondents answer the way people do, including variability, extreme and midpoint answers, acquiescence, consistency and person fit?

Each index will be anchored between a shuffled baseline (0) and a second sample of real people (100). The synthetic authenticity benchmark compares several models in one table, scored by their weakest column by default.

The package compares models and supports decisions about them. It does not show that synthetic respondents can replace a field test.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("okanbulut/synthcheck")

Example 

library(synthcheck)

# Honesty-Humility, Canada: real people and four language models
h <- hexaco_items$item[hexaco_items$trait == "H"]
rev_items <- intersect(h, hexaco_items$item[hexaco_items$reverse])
keyed <- function(d) { d <- d[h]; d[rev_items] <- 8 - d[rev_items]; d }

real <- keyed(hexaco_real[hexaco_real$country == "Canada", ])
ca <- hexaco_llm[hexaco_llm$country == "Canada" & hexaco_llm$attempt <= 4, ]
synthetic <- lapply(split(ca, ca$model, drop = TRUE),
                    function(m) lapply(split(m, m$attempt), keyed))

cov <- synthetic_coverage(synthetic, real, cor = "pearson")
cov
gg_coverage(cov)

Data

hexaco_real holds 17,874 real respondents to the 240 IPIP-HEXACO items from Canada, Great Britain and the United States (Open-Source Psychometrics Project). hexaco_llm holds 59,611 synthetic respondents from four open-weight language models (10 attempts per country), and hexaco_items holds the item text, facets and keys.

Related

synthcheck grew out of the coverage strip in mirtverse. See the article Checking synthetic respondents: The coverage strip.
